assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles turned nucleic-acid drugs from fragile molecules into deliverable medicines (siRNA therapy, then mRNA vaccines). This is a molecular-design solution to a hard delivery problem, built on lipid chemistry and self-assembly, and it clearly changed what clinicians can do. Importance and lasting impact are exceptional.
assessment.attribution: The Vancouver group (Cullis and colleagues) developed ionizable lipid and rapid-mixing LNP formulation; Langer and Anderson contributed lipidoid and combinatorial lipid discovery and the broader delivery concept. The credit is spread across several people and I would expect a debate over who is decisive. Two names is my best compromise.
assessment.maturity: Validated at global scale by approved siRNA (patisiran) and mRNA vaccines, with many independent groups and companies confirming the platform. Recognition is timely and not premature.
uncertainties: Allocation among Cullis, Hope, Madden, MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer is unresolved.
Overlap with the 2023 Physiology or Medicine mRNA prize may raise questions about how the delivery chemistry is framed.
I am relying on memory for details of who invented which lipid generation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Induced-proximity degradation opened a new pharmacological modality: bifunctional PROTACs and molecular glues hijack the ubiquitin-proteasome system to remove proteins that were considered undruggable. It is conceptually original and rests on rational chemical design, with direct clinical consequences.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies established the PROTAC concept, and Ciulli added structure-guided design and VHL ligands. The molecular glue strand (thalidomide mechanism, Handa, Ito, Gray and others) is a distinct, partly separate contribution, so a three-person prize would have to reduce a compound discovery.
assessment.maturity: Many degraders are in clinical trials, but approval of a PROTAC drug is still pending in my knowledge. Chemical-biology validation is strong; the clinical proof is the maturity concern.
uncertainties: Clinical validation is incomplete; timing may be slightly early.
Whether PROTACs and molecular glues are one discovery or two.
Credit between Crews, Deshaies, Ciulli, Sakamoto and the glue-degrader group.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Shokat's tethering of small molecules to the mutant cysteine of KRAS G12C cracked a target long treated as undruggable and led to approved covalent inhibitors. His analog-sensitive kinase chemical genetics is also a lasting tool. This is a clear case of chemistry changing patient care.
assessment.attribution: A single, well-defined laureate: the covalent KRAS strategy and the chemical-genetic kinase work both trace to his laboratory. Clinical development by industry built on his discovery, but the foundational contribution is his.
assessment.maturity: Sotorasib and adrenagrasib are approved and the approach has been replicated broadly, so confirmation is strong. Timing is reasonable.
uncertainties: Whether a single-laureate prize is enough or the committee prefers to pair this with related covalent-drugging work.
Details of the clinical translation are from memory.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Sequencing by synthesis with reversible terminator nucleotides, and the related massively parallel approaches, made genome sequencing cheap and routine. The chemical design of the reversible terminators and clonal cluster methods underlies modern genomics and diagnostics. Impact is enormous.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman conceived and developed the Solexa chemistry that became Illumina sequencing. Rothberg (pyrosequencing, 454), Mayer and Ju contributed related but different platforms, so the allocation is contestable.
assessment.maturity: Dominant technology for roughly two decades, with extensive independent validation. Fully mature.
uncertainties: Competing claims between platform developers.
Whether the committee sees this as chemistry or as genomics technology.
Patent and commercial history may complicate the credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetic code expansion lets researchers encode non-natural amino acids into proteins in living cells through orthogonal tRNA/synthetase pairs. It is a clean, original molecular design principle that gives precise control over protein chemistry, and it is widely used in biophysics, biomaterials and therapeutic protein engineering.
assessment.attribution: Schultz and Wang demonstrated the first orthogonal pair for a non-natural amino acid in vivo, and Chin extended it to animals, multiple codons and new ribosomes. Mehl and Yokoyama contributed important systems, so the trio is a reasonable but not unique choice.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced and applied by hundreds of laboratories over two decades. Mature, with some therapeutic uses emerging.
uncertainties: Which of Schultz, Chin, Wang is more decisive.
Direct clinical impact is still modest compared with higher-ranked candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Mass spectrometry proteomics provides quantitative, large-scale measurement of proteins, modifications and interactions, and it is now central to bioanalytical chemistry and biomarker work. The impact on biology and medicine is broad and lasting.
assessment.attribution: Mann, Aebersold and Yates are the leading figures for shotgun, quantitative and data-driven proteomics. Hunt, Gygi and Heck also made decisive contributions, and the 2002 Chemistry prize (Fenn, Tanaka) already recognised ionization, so overlap and allocation need care.
assessment.maturity: Thoroughly confirmed and ubiquitous. Timing is not an issue.
uncertainties: Large number of deserving contributors.
Part of the ionization foundations has already been recognised, which may reduce novelty for this candidate.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: DNA-programmed nanoparticle assembly and spherical nucleic acids combine Watson-Crick recognition with nanoparticle chemistry to make programmable materials and highly sensitive diagnostic and therapeutic constructs. The molecular-design logic is close to my own area and the translation to diagnostics is real.
assessment.attribution: Mirkin and Alivisatos independently reported DNA-directed nanoparticle assembly in 1996. Mirkin subsequently developed spherical nucleic acids, diagnostics and therapeutics. Storhoff and Mucic are credited co-authors but less likely laureates. Alivisatos is also linked to quantum dots, which were recognised in 2023.
assessment.maturity: The assembly concept is well confirmed; the clinical value of spherical nucleic acids is less settled.
uncertainties: Overlap between Alivisatos and the 2023 quantum-dot prize.
The clinical and commercial impact of spherical nucleic acids is incomplete.
I may be biased toward this area through my own work.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Activity-based protein profiling uses reactive chemical probes to report on the functional state of enzymes in complex proteomes, and it enables target discovery and covalent ligand screening. It is an important tool for chemical biology and drug discovery.
assessment.attribution: Cravatt is the most central figure, with fluorophosphonate probes and competitive profiling. Bogyo, Overkleeft and Weerapana made significant contributions, so a second name is plausible but not obvious.
assessment.maturity: Broadly adopted and mature, with growing links to covalent drug discovery, though less transformative than the higher-ranked options.
uncertainties: Pairing with Bogyo or others is uncertain.
Novelty versus earlier activity-based labeling work (Cravatt's predecessors) is not fully clear to me.
